name: Sumatriptan
route_note: Oral tablets, subcutaneous autoinjector, nasal spray and nasal powder; taken at the onset of an attack.

discovery.by: Patrick Humphrey and colleagues, Glaxo, UK
discovery.note: Designed in the 1970s–80s as a selective agonist at the 5-HT1-like receptor mediating cranial vasoconstriction.

rx_status: prescription (oral OTC in some countries, e.g. UK pharmacy medicine)
tagline: The first triptan, which transformed acute migraine treatment
summary: Sumatriptan, the first triptan, is a selective serotonin 5-HT1B/1D agonist that relieves acute migraine and cluster headache attacks. Its subcutaneous form is one of the fastest-acting migraine treatments.
mechanism: Sumatriptan activates 5-HT1B receptors on dilated meningeal blood vessels, causing vasoconstriction, and 5-HT1D receptors on trigeminal nerve terminals, inhibiting release of CGRP and other inflammatory neuropeptides.
It may also inhibit transmission in the trigeminal nucleus caudalis. Vasoconstriction of coronary arteries underlies its contraindication in ischaemic heart disease.
uses: Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura
Acute treatment of cluster headache (subcutaneous and nasal)

history.title: First launch
history.detail: Glaxo launches sumatriptan (Imigran) in Europe, starting with the Netherlands.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Imitrex injection; tablets follow in 1995 and nasal spray in 1997.

history.title: UK pharmacy availability
history.detail: Low-dose sumatriptan tablets become available without prescription from UK pharmacies.

history.title: Treximet and generics
history.detail: A sumatriptan/naproxen combination is approved; generic sumatriptan launches in the US in 2008–2009.

history.title: New delivery devices
history.detail: The FDA approves a breath-powered nasal powder (Onzetra Xsail) and a needle-based autoinjector (Zembrace).

history.title: Tosymra
history.detail: A nasal spray with a permeation enhancer is approved in the US.

pk.excretion: renal and faecal, mainly as indole acetic acid metabolite

serious: Myocardial ischaemia, infarction and coronary vasospasm

facts: Sumatriptan's development was based on the observation that serotonin infusions could abort migraine attacks but caused intolerable side effects.
